view.stem: One box contains 10 pairs of brown socks and 10 pairs of black socks. Another contains 10 pairs of brown gloves and 10 pairs of black gloves. All socks have the same size, and all gloves have the same size. Items are taken without looking. The aim is to obtain a same-color pair of socks and a same-color pair of gloves. Which claims about guaranteed pairs and possible draws are true?

options.text: Taking 3 socks guarantees a same-color sock pair.
Taking 3 gloves guarantees a same-color glove pair.
Taking 20 gloves can produce only left-hand gloves.
Taking 2 socks guarantees a same-color sock pair.
Taking 21 gloves guarantees a same-color glove pair.

view.stem: A cyclist travels between two cities at 10 km/h. At 12 km/h the cyclist would arrive 4 hours earlier. What is the distance between the cities?
Stations A and B are 46 km apart. A group leaves A toward B at 5 km/h. Two hours later another group leaves B toward A at 4 km/h. How long after the second group departs do they meet?

A tram passenger notices a friend walking along the tram route in the opposite direction. After 10 seconds the passenger gets off and pursues the friend. The passenger walks twice as fast as the friend; the tram travels five times as fast as the passenger walks. The original task asks how many seconds the pursuit takes. Let the friend's speed be u. Which relative-speed claims follow from the supplied speed ratios?

options.text: While the passenger is aboard, the tram and friend have relative speed 10u.
During pursuit, the passenger closes a positive gap at speed u.
During pursuit, the passenger closes a positive gap at speed 3u.
While the passenger is aboard, the tram and friend have relative speed 11u.

view.stem: A motorcyclist travels from city A to city B. At 35 km/h the arrival would be 2 hours late; at 50 km/h it would be 1 hour early. Which conclusions about the distance and the travel time needed for an on-time arrival are true?

options.text: The travel time needed for an on-time arrival is 12 hours.
The distance between the cities is 350 km.
The travel time needed for an on-time arrival is 8 hours.
The distance between the cities is 350/3 km.

view.stem: A train takes 45 seconds to pass a 450 m bridge and 15 seconds to pass a signal cabin. The original task asks for the train's length and speed. Let its length be L metres and its constant speed be v metres per second. Which equation models the complete passage of the train over the bridge?

A train needs 10 hours to travel from station A to station B. If its speed were 10 km/h faster, it could cover the route within 8 hours. The original task asks for its speed and the distance. Let the original speed be v>0 km/h. Which inequality is an equivalent model of the faster journey's stated 'within 8 hours' requirement?

A skier calculates that travelling at 10 km/h would give an arrival at 1 p.m., while travelling at 15 km/h would give an arrival at 11 a.m. The skier wants to arrive at noon. Which conclusions about this journey are true?

options.text: The required speed for a noon arrival is 12 km/h.
The common departure time is 7 a.m.
The required speed for a noon arrival is 12.5 km/h.

view.stem: Alex and Lena each receive a coat, shoes, and a hat, costing $75 altogether. Each of Alex's items costs 1.5 times the corresponding item for Lena. Alex's coat costs 10 times Alex's hat and 3 times the price of Lena's shoes and hat. The original task asks for all six prices. What is the price of Lena's hat?
On the first day a mowing team cuts half a meadow plus 2 hectares. On the second day it cuts 25% of the remaining area and the final 6 hectares. What is the meadow's area?
A harvest of mushrooms weighs 100 kg and is 99% water. After some drying, the water proportion is 98%. What is the weight after drying?

A bus traveller first sees a two-digit number on a mileage marker. One hour later the marker number has three digits: its hundreds digit is the earlier units digit, its tens digit is zero, and its units digit is the earlier tens digit. Two hours after that three-digit observation, only its zero digit has changed to another digit. The original task asks for the bus speed. Write the successive readings as 10a+b, 100b+a, and 100b+10c+a, where a, b, c are digits from 1 to 9. Which changes in the marker numbers follow from these digit conditions?

A traveller must cross an 80 km desert, walks 20 km per day, and can carry at most three days' food and water. The traveller must establish a station on the route to store provisions. The original task asks how many days the crossing takes. Let the station be x kilometres from the starting end. On the final departure from that station toward the far end, no further provisions are obtained. Which inequality is equivalent to applying the three-day carrying limit to that entire final leg?

A city's residents consist of people who speak only English, people who speak only Spanish, and people who speak both. Spanish speakers are 85% of the residents and English speakers are 75%. What percentage speak both languages?
Share 7 apples equally among 12 people. No apple may be cut into five or more pieces. Which plan meets both the equal-share and per-apple cutting conditions?

options.text: Cut 6 apples into halves and 1 into twelfths; give each person one half and one twelfth.
Cut 3 apples into thirds and 4 into quarters; give each person one third and one quarter.
Cut 3 apples into quarters and 4 into thirds; give each person one quarter and one third.

view.stem: Cut a 600 g cake into pieces so that the same cut pieces can be shared equally among 3 people or, alternatively, among 4 people. Pieces need not all have equal weights, and the sharing uses whole cut pieces without cutting them again. What is the minimum number of pieces?

Starting with a full cup of coffee, I drink 1/6 of a cup and refill it with milk. I then drink 1/3 of a cup and refill with milk, drink half a cup and refill with milk, and finally drink the entire cup. Which comparison of the total amounts consumed is correct?

options.text: More milk than coffee was consumed.
More coffee than milk was consumed.
Equal amounts of coffee and milk were consumed.

view.stem: The fraction m/n is in lowest terms. The original task asks whether m/(n+m), m/(n+mn), and n/(2*n+3n) can be reduced. Judge the following claims only where the displayed fraction has a nonzero denominator; no extra restriction on m or n is supplied. Which claims are true?

options.text: Where its denominator is nonzero, m/(n+m) is necessarily in lowest terms.
Where its denominator is nonzero, n/(2*n+3n) necessarily admits a nontrivial reduction.
Where its denominator is nonzero, m/(n+mn) is necessarily in lowest terms.

view.stem: Ben eats one third of all the apples plus 2 apples. Jamie eats one quarter of all the apples plus 1 apple. Cole eats half of what remains. The final remainder is one sixth of the original total. How many apples were there originally?
Reduce the fractions 37,373,737/81,818,181 and 609,609,609/205,205,205 to lowest terms. Which proposed results are correct?
Consider the fraction (382 + 498*381)/(382*498 - 116). Which comparison of its numerator and denominator determines its value?

options.text: The numerator is 116 less than the denominator.
The numerator and denominator are equal.
The numerator is 498 greater than the denominator.
The numerator is 382 less than the denominator.
